title: A factor 1.10 summary bound excludes passive transfer reciprocity in 68 of 135 selected Allen mouse cell pairs
abstract: We tested whether electrical coupling and input resistance summaries in Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1 can meet passive transfer reciprocity. The necessary rule is k12 R1 = k21 R2. If each of the four positive summaries can change by a factor from 1/f to f, the rule is impossible when the absolute log product ratio exceeds 4 log(f). At f = 1.10, 68 of 135 selected mouse pairs failed. The median minimum factor was 1.10677. Only 2 of 18 pairs failed when both pulse correlation p-values were below 0.01. Using steady resistance gave 67 failures among 135 pairs. The bounds are assumptions, not measured errors. Separate pulse windows, regression slopes, resistance estimates, active currents, and selection prevent a claim of junction rectification. One valid human pair cannot support a species test. Original code, a proof, aggregate results, a figure, exact source hashes, and external retrieval steps support reproduction. Source records and external code are not bundled.

display.caption: Share of selected mouse pairs that cannot meet passive transfer reciprocity within the stated common factor for four summaries. Curves use different selection or resistance rules. The bounds do not estimate measurement error.
